c.tagline: India's maximum city, where Bollywood dreams meet colonial grandeur and the Arabian Sea.

taxi.fareNote: The iconic black-and-yellow 'kaali-peeli' cabs and auto-rickshaws (suburbs only, not South Mumbai) run on meters; insist the meter is used, or book via Uber/Ola for a fixed fare.

emergency.note: 112 is the all-in-one national emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance.

avoid.reason: Generally safe; pickpocketing on local trains and around Colaba/CST; begging and "friendship" scams

hood_desc: The southern tourist heart around the Gateway of India and the Taj hotel, packed with heritage buildings, cafes, street stalls, and the Colaba Causeway market; best for first-timers who want the icons on their doorstep.
Mumbai's grand Victorian-Gothic and Art Deco business core around CSMT station, Kala Ghoda, and Flora Fountain; walkable, full of museums, galleries, and colonial architecture.
The trendy suburban hub of leafy lanes, seaside promenades, indie boutiques, cafes, and buzzing bars; the city's creative and celebrity set gravitates here.
A relaxed coastal suburb built around a long sandy beach, upscale homes, and beachfront hotels; favored by families and Bollywood stars wanting sea air away from the crush.
A revamped former textile-mill district now dense with rooftop bars, clubs, fine-dining, malls, and skyscrapers along the Worli seafront; the go-to for nightlife and modern dining.
lodging: Salvation Army Red Shield Guest House

water.note: Tap water is not safe for visitors; use bottled or filtered water, including for brushing teeth.

transit.hours: Suburban trains run roughly 4:00 AM to 1:00 AM; metro lines about 5:30 AM to 11:30 PM; BEST buses run all day with limited night services.
transit.note: The suburban railway is the city's lifeline, moving millions daily on Western, Central, and Harbour lines; an expanding metro network, a monorail, and BEST buses fill in the gaps, with ride-hailing and kaali-peeli taxis for the rest.
transit.pay: Paper tickets and smart cards for trains; metro uses tokens, QR tickets, and the Mumbai 1 card; BEST buses take cash or the Chalo app/card. There is no single fully-unified fare card as of 2026.

ferry: Ferries to Elephanta Island from the Gateway of India
train: Long-distance Indian Railways from CSMT, Mumbai Central, Dadar, and LTT

transit.m: Airport Metro (Line 3/Line 7) plus suburban rail into the city
Prepaid taxi or Uber/Ola to South Mumbai (45-90 min in traffic)
BEST AC bus to nearby suburbs and rail stations

tip.r: Not obligatory; 5-10% at restaurants when no service charge is added, and rounding up for taxis, autos, and porters is appreciated.

food.name: Vada pav
food.desc: Spiced potato fritter crushed into a soft bun with dry garlic chutney and a fried green chilli. Mumbai's original commuter lunch.

places.name: Ashok Vada Pav
places.note: Legendary stall by Kirti College; queues form from mid-morning for the hot batches.

places.name: Aaram Vada Pav
places.note: Opposite CSMT station since the 1930s, a fixture for office workers and travellers.

places.name: Aaswad
places.note: Maharashtrian institution whose vada pav has won awards abroad; also famous for misal pav.

food.name: Pav bhaji
food.desc: Mashed spiced vegetables griddled with butter and served with pav rolls toasted in more butter, plus raw onion and lime.

places.name: Sardar Pav Bhaji
places.note: The city's most famous plate, notorious for its enormous slab of butter.

places.name: Cannon Pav Bhaji
places.note: Streetside counter beside CSMT, fast turnover and open until late evening.

places.name: Amar Juice Centre
places.note: Suburban favourite doing cheese and Punjabi variations alongside the classic.

food.name: Bhel puri and sev puri
food.desc: Puffed rice or crisp puris tossed with onion, tomato, potato, tamarind and mint chutneys - Mumbai chaat, mixed to order in seconds.

places.name: Girgaum Chowpatty stalls
places.note: The seafront chaat row at sunset is the classic Mumbai bhel puri experience.

places.name: Elco Market
places.note: Long-running chaat address with hygienic prep and a wide street-food menu.

places.name: Kailash Parbat
places.note: Sit-down Sindhi restaurant serving chaat since 1952, good if you want air conditioning.

food.name: Bombay sandwich
food.desc: Cold sandwich of cucumber, tomato, beetroot, potato and green chutney, either plain or griddled with cheese and butter into a toastie.

places.name: Elco Market
places.note: Reliable version of the grilled cheese variant alongside the chaat counter.

places.name: Flora Fountain sandwich carts
places.note: Office-district carts assembling sandwiches to order all through the working day.

places.name: Kailash Parbat
places.note: Sit-down option near the Gateway with the full range of grilled sandwiches.

food.name: Keema pav
food.desc: Spiced minced mutton, often finished with a fried egg, mopped up with buttered pav. A cornerstone of Mumbai's Irani and Muslim cafes.

places.name: Olympia Coffee House
places.note: Marble-and-mirror Irani cafe from 1918; keema pav and breakfast served daily.

places.name: Sarvi Restaurant
places.note: Open since 1921 and still known across the city for its keema and seekh kebabs.

places.name: Noor Mohammadi Hotel
places.note: Century-old kitchen famed for nalli nihari as well as its keema.

food.name: Bombil fry and koliwada seafood
food.desc: Koli fisherfolk cooking: Bombay duck floured and fried, prawns in a red koliwada batter, and coconut-thick surmai curry with rice.

places.name: Gajalee
places.note: Coastal Malvani specialist; the crab and bombil fry are what people come for.

places.name: Trishna
places.note: Long-celebrated seafood restaurant behind the Jehangir gallery; book ahead.

places.name: Mahesh Lunch Home
places.note: Mangalorean seafood institution serving the city since 1977, busy at lunch.

food.name: Cutting chai
food.desc: Half a glass of strong milky tea boiled with ginger and cardamom, drunk fast and often. The rhythm-keeper of the Mumbai working day.

places.name: Yazdani Bakery
places.note: Irani bakery famed for brun maska and ginger biscuits; mostly a takeaway counter now.

places.name: Kyani and Co.
places.note: Trading since 1904, one of the last true Irani cafes with bun maska and chai.

places.name: Sassanian Boulangerie
places.note: Irani bakery-cafe trading since 1913, famous for mawa cakes alongside the chai.

food.name: Falooda
food.desc: Layered rose-syrup milk drink with vermicelli, basil seeds and ice cream, drunk with a spoon and a straw. Summer relief in a tall glass.

places.name: Badshah Cold Drinks
places.note: Serving falooda since 1905; the single most famous glass in the city.

places.name: Haji Ali Juice Centre
places.note: Open late by the causeway, known for fruit creams and heavy-duty faloodas.

places.name: Taj Ice Cream
places.note: Hand-churned ice creams since 1887, excellent as a falooda topping.

landmarks: Gateway of India
The colossal basalt arch overlooking the Arabian Sea is Mumbai's defining monument and most-photographed waterfront icon.
Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CST)
A UNESCO World Heritage Victorian Gothic railway station whose ornate spires and domes make it one of India's most photographed buildings.
Marine Drive
The sweeping seafront boulevard known as the 'Queen's Necklace' for the glittering arc of lights along its curve at night.
Haji Ali Dargah
A dazzling white mosque and tomb perched on an islet, connected to the mainland by a causeway that vanishes at high tide.
Siddhivinayak Temple
One of India's most revered and visited Ganesh temples, drawing huge crowds of devotees and instantly recognizable golden dome.
Elephanta Caves
Ancient rock-cut cave temples dedicated to Shiva on an island a short ferry ride from the Gateway of India, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Bandra-Worli Sea Link
A sleek cable-stayed bridge arcing across the Arabian Sea that has become a modern symbol of Mumbai, especially striking at sunset.
Dhobi Ghat
The world's largest open-air laundry, a maze of concrete wash-pens that offers a uniquely chaotic, colorful photo opportunity.
Taj Mahal Palace Hotel
A grand Indo-Saracenic dome-topped hotel beside the Gateway of India, an emblem of old-world Mumbai glamour.
Colaba Causeway
Mumbai's bustling colonial-era shopping street packed with street stalls, cafes, and heritage architecture in the historic Colaba district.

train.note: India runs no international passenger trains from Mumbai - the Delhi-Lahore Samjhauta Express has been suspended since 2019. Long-distance trains use Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) for central and southern routes, Mumbai Central for Gujarat, Rajasthan and Delhi, and Lokmanya Tilak Terminus in the eastern suburbs. Book on IRCTC, which opens 60 days ahead and needs an account with an Indian or international mobile number; premium Rajdhani and Vande Bharat services sell out fastest. Foreign tourists can also use the small tourist quota at CSMT's international tourist bureau.

bus.note: There are no international coaches from Mumbai. Long-distance buses leave from Dadar, Borivali and Sion rather than one central terminal, and the state operator MSRTC (https://msrtc.maharashtra.gov.in/) plus private sleeper operators cover Goa, Pune, Bengaluru and Ahmedabad. Almost everyone books through the aggregator redBus (https://www.redbus.in/), which lists all the private operators in one place. Overnight AC sleeper coaches to Goa take 12-14 hours.

intl.to: Elephanta Island (India) - from the Gateway of India, ~1 hr
intl.op: Maharashtra Tourism launch operators — tickets at the Gateway jetty

intl.to: Mandwa & Alibaug (India) - fast catamaran across the harbour, ~20 min

ferry.note: There are no international sailings from Mumbai; the port handles cargo and the occasional cruise call. The Elephanta launches leave the Gateway of India through the day and are suspended during the monsoon, roughly June to September. M2M's air-conditioned catamaran to Mandwa runs year-round from Bhaucha Dhakka (Ferry Wharf) and carries cars, cutting hours off the road to Alibaug.

half.name: Lonavala
half.blurb: A hill town in the Sahyadri range with waterfalls, forts, and a fudge-making tradition, popular during monsoon season.

half.name: Alibaug
half.blurb: A coastal town across Mumbai harbor reached by ferry, with beaches and the 17th-century sea fort of Kolaba.

full.name: Matheran
full.blurb: A vehicle-free hill station reached by a narrow-gauge toy train, with red-earth trails and viewpoints over the Western Ghats.

full.name: Nashik
full.blurb: India's wine capital, with Sula and other vineyards offering tastings and tours in the Nashik valley.
